rationale: Continuing the authorized source work on the deferred transport surface: reading the TCP stream layer, the stream-context lifecycle and the in-process peer registration, and correcting one item I had listed in the previous feedback without having read it. Reading only; no defect asserted, no obligation created.

feedback.answered: Three more parts are now sourced. TCP stream layer: newTCPTransport binds with net.Listen("tcp", bindAddr), wraps the listener in TCPStreamLayer with an optional advertise address, rejects a non-TCP listener address (errNotTCP) or an unspecified/absent advertise address (errNotAdvertisable) before creating the transport through a creator callback, and Dial/Accept/Close/Addr are plain net.DialTimeout/listener delegation with Addr preferring the advertised address (tcp_transport.go 23-117). Correction: the TLS configuration item I listed previously was an assumption, not a reading; there is no TLS code in the captured library (no NetworkTransportConfig.TLSConfig and no tls package use outside tests), so TLS can only come from a caller-supplied StreamLayer, and that item is withdrawn rather than left as an unread library responsibility. Stream context: setupStreamContext creates a cancellable context, getStreamContext reads it under its lock, and CloseStreams releases every pooled connection and then cancels and recreates the context under both the pool and context locks, with the code's own comment that the ordering is required so handlers cannot end up holding a never-cancellable context (net_transport.go 285-331); Close closes shutdownCh and the stream layer once (333-345). In-process registration: Connect/Disconnect/DisconnectAll mutate the peers map under the transport lock, and Disconnect additionally closes and compacts any pipelines registered for that peer (inmem_transport.go 215-250).
remaining: The in-process peer consumer-channel capacity was not read, so how many in-process RPCs can queue before a send blocks is still unknown.
Whether an address-provider change can race an in-flight dial was read only at the level of the address lock in getProviderAddressOrFallback.
The heartbeat classification read earlier was not re-checked against exactly what the leader's heartbeat goroutine emits.

StreamLayer implementations supplied by callers remain outside the library; anything a caller wraps around TCPStreamLayer is not a library responsibility, but no library-side TLS or stream-wrapping helper exists to map.

Previously recorded open items are unchanged: installSnapshot watermark reachability from a legal leader history, the compacted-leader variant of the truncation-failure case, and execution corroboration of the two reading-based consequences.
